claim: Liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) involving intrinsically disordered protein regions (IDRs) is a major physical mechanism for biological membraneless compartmentalization.
source: Liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) involving intrinsically disordered protein regions (IDRs) is a major physical mechanism for biological membraneless compartmentalization.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific consensus in the field of biomolecular condensates.

claim: Caprin1 exhibits salt-dependent reentrant phase behaviors.
source: The multifaceted electrostatic effects in these biomolecular condensates are exemplified here by experimental and theoretical investigations of the different salt- and ATP-dependent LLPSs of an IDR of messenger RNA-regulating protein Caprin1 and its phosphorylated variant pY-Caprin1, exhibiting, for example, reentrant behaviors in some instances but not others.
evidence: The abstract states that experimental and theoretical investigations demonstrate reentrant behaviors for Caprin1 under certain conditions.

claim: pY-Caprin1 does not exhibit reentrant phase behaviors under the same conditions as Caprin1.
source: The multifaceted electrostatic effects in these biomolecular condensates are exemplified here by experimental and theoretical investigations of the different salt- and ATP-dependent LLPSs of an IDR of messenger RNA-regulating protein Caprin1 and its phosphorylated variant pY-Caprin1, exhibiting, for example, reentrant behaviors in some instances but not others.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states that reentrant behaviors occur in some instances but not others, referring to differences between Caprin1 and pY-Caprin1.

claim: Interchain ion bridges enhance LLPS of polyelectrolytes such as Caprin1.
source: Experimental data are rationalized by physical modeling using analytical theory, molecular dynamics, and polymer field-theoretic simulations, indicating that interchain ion bridges enhance LLPS of polyelectrolytes such as Caprin1 and the high valency of ATP-magnesium is a significant factor for its colocalization with the condensed phases, as similar trends are observed for other IDRs.
evidence: The abstract states that modeling indicates interchain ion bridges enhance LLPS of polyelectrolytes like Caprin1.

claim: The high valency of ATP-magnesium is a significant factor for its colocalization with condensed phases.
source: Experimental data are rationalized by physical modeling using analytical theory, molecular dynamics, and polymer field-theoretic simulations, indicating that interchain ion bridges enhance LLPS of polyelectrolytes such as Caprin1 and the high valency of ATP-magnesium is a significant factor for its colocalization with the condensed phases, as similar trends are observed for other IDRs.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states that modeling indicates high valency of ATP-magnesium is significant for colocalization.

claim: Electrostatics plays major roles in biophysical and biochemical processes.
source: Electrostatics plays major roles in biophysical and biochemical processes (Honig and Nicholls, 1995; Zhou and Pang, 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Electrostatics is particularly important for IDR LLPS because of the relatively high compositions of charge residues in IDRs.
source: Because of the relatively high compositions of charge residues in IDRs, electrostatics is particularly important for IDR LLPS (Nott et al., 2015; Lin et al., 2016), which is often also facilitated by π-related interactions (Wang et al., 2018; Vernon et al., 2018), hydrophobicity, and hydrogen bonding (Murthy et al., 2019; Cai et al., 2022), and is modulated by temperature (Lin et al., 2018; Dignon et al., 2019a), hydrostatic pressure (Cinar et al., 2019; Cinar et al., 2020), osmolytes (Cinar et al., 2019), RNA (Maharana et al., 2018; Tsang et al., 2019; Dutagaci et al., 2021; Laghmach et al., 2022), salt, pH (Wang et al., 2017), molecular crowding (André and Spruijt, 2020; Patel et al., 2022; Kumari et al., 2024), and post-translational modifications (PTMs; Shin and Brangwynne, 2017; Kim et al., 2019; Owen and Shewmaker, 2019; Snead and Gladfelter, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations and is based on established knowledge about IDR composition.

claim: IDR LLPS is often facilitated by π-related interactions.
source: Because of the relatively high compositions of charge residues in IDRs, electrostatics is particularly important for IDR LLPS (Nott et al., 2015; Lin et al., 2016), which is often also facilitated by π-related interactions (Wang et al., 2018; Vernon et al., 2018), hydrophobicity, and hydrogen bonding (Murthy et al., 2019; Cai et al., 2022), and is modulated by temperature (Lin et al., 2018; Dignon et al., 2019a), hydrostatic pressure (Cinar et al., 2019; Cinar et al., 2020), osmolytes (Cinar et al., 2019), RNA (Maharana et al., 2018; Tsang et al., 2019; Dutagaci et al., 2021; Laghmach et al., 2022), salt, pH (Wang et al., 2017), molecular crowding (André and Spruijt, 2020; Patel et al., 2022; Kumari et al., 2024), and post-translational modifications (PTMs; Shin and Brangwynne, 2017; Kim et al., 2019; Owen and Shewmaker, 2019; Snead and Gladfelter, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Some IDRs undergo reentrant phase separation when temperature, pressure, salt, RNA, or concentrations of small molecules is varied.
source: Intriguingly, some IDRs undergo reentrant phase separation (Cinar et al., 2019) or dissolution (Banerjee et al., 2017) when temperature, pressure (Cinar et al., 2019), salt (Krainer et al., 2021; Hong et al., 2022), RNA (Banerjee et al., 2017; Alshareedah et al., 2019), or concentrations of small molecules such as heparin (Babinchak et al., 2020) is varied.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to experimental studies.

claim: ATP hydrolysis is utilized to synthesize or break chemical bonds and drive transport to regulate 'active liquid' properties such as concentration gradients and droplet sizes.
source: As energy currency, ATP hydrolysis is utilized to synthesize or break chemical bonds and drive transport to regulate 'active liquid' properties such as concentration gradients and droplet sizes (Wurtz and Lee, 2018; Bertrand and Lee, 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: ATP can influence biomolecular LLPS without hydrolysis.
source: ATP can also influence biomolecular LLPS without hydrolysis, akin to other LLPS promoters or suppressors (Nguemaha and Zhou, 2018; Ghosh et al., 2019) that are effectively ligands of the condensate scaffold (Ruff et al., 2021), or through ATP's effect on lowering free [Mg2+] (Wright et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: ATP acts as an amphiphilic hydrotrope with intracellular concentrations much higher than that required for an energy source.
source: Notably, as an amphiphilic hydrotrope (Martins et al., 2022) with intracellular concentrations much higher than that required for an energy source, ATP is also seen to afford an important function independent of hydrolysis by solubilizing proteins, preventing LLPS and destabilizing aggregates, as exemplified by measurements on several proteins including fused in sarcoma (FUS) (Patel et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: ATP prevents LLPS and destabilizes aggregates of FUS.
source: Notably, as an amphiphilic hydrotrope (Martins et al., 2022) with intracellular concentrations much higher than that required for an energy source, ATP is also seen to afford an important function independent of hydrolysis by solubilizing proteins, preventing LLPS and destabilizing aggregates, as exemplified by measurements on several proteins including fused in sarcoma (FUS) (Patel et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to experimental work on FUS.

claim: ATP promotes LLPS of an IgG1 antibody.
source: For instance, ATP promotes, not suppresses, LLPS of an IgG1 antibody (Tian and Qian, 2021), basic IDPs (Kota et al., 2024), and enhances LLPS of full-length and the C-terminal domain (CTD) of FUS at low [ATP] but prevents LLPS at high [ATP] (Kang et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to experimental work.

claim: ATP enhances LLPS of full-length and the C-terminal domain (CTD) of FUS at low [ATP] but prevents LLPS at high [ATP].
source: For instance, ATP promotes, not suppresses, LLPS of an IgG1 antibody (Tian and Qian, 2021), basic IDPs (Kota et al., 2024), and enhances LLPS of full-length and the C-terminal domain (CTD) of FUS at low [ATP] but prevents LLPS at high [ATP] (Kang et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to experimental work showing reentrant behavior.

claim: The 103-residue Caprin1 is a highly charged IDR with 19 charged residues.
source: The 103-residue Caprin1 is a highly charged IDR with 19 charged residues [Figure 1a and Appendix 1, Appendix 1—figure 1]: 15 R, 1 K, and 3 aspartic acids (D); fraction of charged residues = 19/103 = 0.184 and NCPR = 13/103 = 0.126.
evidence: This claim is based on sequence analysis of Caprin1 and is illustrated in Figure 1a.

claim: Caprin1 has a fraction of charged residues of 0.184 and NCPR of 0.126.
source: The 103-residue Caprin1 is a highly charged IDR with 19 charged residues [Figure 1a and Appendix 1, Appendix 1—figure 1]: 15 R, 1 K, and 3 aspartic acids (D); fraction of charged residues = 19/103 = 0.184 and NCPR = 13/103 = 0.126.
evidence: This is a direct calculation from the sequence composition.

claim: Caprin1 behaves like chemically synthesized polyelectrolytes.
source: With a substantial positive net charge, Caprin1's phase behaviors are markedly different from those of polyampholytic IDRs with nearly zero net charge such as Ddx4 to which early sequence-specific LLPS theories were targeted (Nott et al., 2015; Lin et al., 2016). Instead, Caprin1 behaves like chemically synthesized polyelectrolytes (Dobrynin and Rubinstein, 2005).
evidence: This is an inference based on the charge properties of Caprin1 and comparison with polyelectrolyte theory.

claim: When most or all of the 7 tyrosines in the Caprin1 IDR are phosphorylated, negative charges are added to produce a near-net-neutral polyampholyte.
source: In contrast, when most or all of the 7 tyrosines (Y) in the Caprin1 IDR are phosphorylated (pY), negative charges are added to produce a near-net-neutral polyampholyte.
evidence: This is based on the known charge of phosphorylated tyrosines and the sequence composition.

claim: The experimental sample of highly phosphorylated Caprin1 consists mainly of a mixture of IDRs with 6 or 7 phosphorylations.
source: Mass spectrometry indicates that the experimental sample of highly phosphorylated Caprin1 consists mainly of a mixture of IDRs with 6 or 7 phosphorylations (Appendix 1—figure 2).
evidence: This claim is based on mass spectrometry data shown in Appendix 1—figure 2.

claim: Model pY-Caprin1 has a NCPR of −0.00971.
source: Accordingly, since the charge of a pY is ≈ –2 at the experimental pH = 7.4, –14 charges are added to Caprin1 for our model pY-Caprin1, resulting in a polyampholyte with a very small NCPR = −1/103 = −0.00971 (Figure 1b).
evidence: This is a direct calculation based on the charge of phosphorylated tyrosines and the Caprin1 sequence.

claim: Caprin1 undergoes LLPS below 20 °C with 100 mM NaCl.
source: The rG-RPA+FH results in Figure 1c indicate that (i) Caprin1 undergoes LLPS below 20 °C with 100 mM NaCl, and that (ii) LLPS propensity, quantified by the upper critical solution temperature (UCST), increases with [NaCl].
evidence: This is a prediction from rG-RPA+FH theory shown in Figure 1c.

claim: LLPS propensity of Caprin1 increases with [NaCl].
source: The rG-RPA+FH results in Figure 1c indicate that (i) Caprin1 undergoes LLPS below 20 °C with 100 mM NaCl, and that (ii) LLPS propensity, quantified by the upper critical solution temperature (UCST), increases with [NaCl].
evidence: This is a prediction from rG-RPA+FH theory shown in Figure 1c and is consistent with experiment.

claim: Caprin1 does not phase separate at room temperature without salt, ATP, RNA, or other proteins.
source: These predictions are consistent with experimental data, including the observation that Caprin1 does not phase separate at room temperature without salt, ATP, RNA, or other proteins, though Caprin1 LLPS can be triggered by adding wildtype (WT) and phosphorylated FMRP and/or RNA (overall [Caprin1] ≳ 10 μM) (Kim et al., 2019), NaCl (Wong et al., 2020), or ATP (overall [Caprin1] = 400 μM) (Kim et al., 2021).
evidence: This is an experimental observation cited from prior work.

claim: Caprin1 LLPS can be triggered by adding wildtype (WT) and phosphorylated FMRP and/or RNA.
source: These predictions are consistent with experimental data, including the observation that Caprin1 does not phase separate at room temperature without salt, ATP, RNA, or other proteins, though Caprin1 LLPS can be triggered by adding wildtype (WT) and phosphorylated FMRP and/or RNA (overall [Caprin1] ≳ 10 μM) (Kim et al., 2019), NaCl (Wong et al., 2020), or ATP (overall [Caprin1] = 400 μM) (Kim et al., 2021).
evidence: This is an experimental observation cited from prior work.

claim: pY-Caprin1 LLPS propensity decreases with increasing [NaCl].
source: In contrast, rG-RPA+FH results in Figure 1d for pY-Caprin1 shows decreasing LLPS propensity with increasing [NaCl], consistent with experimental data and the expected salt dependence of LLPS of nearly net-neutral polyampholytic IDRs such as Ddx4 (Lin et al., 2016).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1d and is consistent with experimental data.

claim: When [Na+] is increased, Caprin1 starts to phase separate at a small [Na+] ≲ 0.1 M, with LLPS propensity increasing to a maximum at [Na+] ∼ 1 M before decreasing at higher [Na+].
source: When [Na+] is increased, the system starts to phase separate at a small [Na+] ≲ 0.1 M, with LLPS propensity increasing to a maximum at [Na+] ∼ 1 M before decreasing at higher [Na+], in agreement with experiment (Figure 3a, blue data points) and consistent with Caprin1 LLPS propensity increasing with [NaCl] from 0.1 to 0.5 M (Figure 1c).
evidence: This is a prediction from rG-RPA shown in Figure 2a and is consistent with experimental data in Figure 3a.

claim: The predicted reentrant dissolution of Caprin1 condensate at high [Na+] is consistent with measurement up to [Na+] ≈ 4.6 M.
source: The predicted reentrant dissolution of Caprin1 condensate at high [Na+] in Figure 2a is consistent with measurement up to [Na+] ≈ 4.6 M indicating a significant decrease in LLPS propensity when [Na+] ≳ 2.5 M (Figure 3a), though the gradual decreasing trend suggests that complete dissolution of condensed droplets is not likely even when NaCl reaches its saturation concentration of ∼6 M.
evidence: This is a comparison between rG-RPA prediction in Figure 2a and experimental data in Figure 3a.

claim: The negative tieline slopes in Figure 2a and b predict that Na+ is partially excluded from the Caprin1 condensate.
source: The negative tieline slopes in Figure 2a and b predict that Na+ is partially excluded from the Caprin1 condensate. This 'salt partitioning' is most likely caused by Caprin1's net positive charge and is consistent with published research on polyelectrolytes with monovalent salt (Shen and Wang, 2018; Eisenberg and Mohan, 1959; Zhang et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a prediction from rG-RPA shown in Figure 2a and b.

claim: The rG-RPA predicted trend of Na+ depletion in Caprin1 condensate is consistent with experiment showing significantly reduced [Na+] in the Caprin1-condensed phase compared to the Caprin1-dilute phase.
source: Here, the rG-RPA predicted trend is consistent with our experiment showing significantly reduced [Na+] in the Caprin1-condensed phase compared to the Caprin1-dilute phase (Table 1), although the larger experimental reduction of [Na+] in the Caprin1 condensed droplet relative to our theoretical prediction remains to be elucidated.
evidence: This is a comparison between rG-RPA prediction and experimental data in Table 1.

claim: [Na+] is consistently lower in the Caprin1-condensed phase than in the Caprin1-dilute phase at two measured temperatures.
source: Consistent with theory, [Na+] is consistently lower in the Caprin1-condensed phase for two temperatures at which the measurements were performed.
evidence: This is stated in the caption of Table 1 and is experimental data.

claim: For near-neutral, very slightly negative model pY-Caprin1, rG-RPA predicts LLPS at [Na+] ≈ 0.
source: In contrast, for the near-neutral, very slightly negative model pY-Caprin1 (Figure 2c and d), rG-RPA predicts LLPS at [Na+] ≈ 0, and the positive tieline slopes indicate that [Na+] is higher in the condensed than in the dilute phase.
evidence: This is a prediction from rG-RPA shown in Figure 2c and d.

claim: For pY-Caprin1, the positive tieline slopes indicate that [Na+] is higher in the condensed than in the dilute phase.
source: In contrast, for the near-neutral, very slightly negative model pY-Caprin1 (Figure 2c and d), rG-RPA predicts LLPS at [Na+] ≈ 0, and the positive tieline slopes indicate that [Na+] is higher in the condensed than in the dilute phase.
evidence: This is a prediction from rG-RPA shown in Figure 2c and d.

claim: The maximum condensed-phase [Caprin1] at low [Na+] is lower with monovalent than with divalent counterions.
source: Other predicted differences between monovalent (Figure 2a and b) and divalent (Figure 2e and f) counterions' impact on Caprin1 LLPS include: (i) The maximum condensed-phase [Caprin1] at low [Na+] is lower with monovalent than with divalent counterions ([Caprin1] ∼ 40 mM vs. ∼ 70 mM).
evidence: This is a prediction from rG-RPA comparing Figure 2a,b with Figure 2e,f.

claim: The [Na+] at the commencement of reentrance is much higher with monovalent than with divalent counterions.
source: (ii) The [Na+] at the commencement of reentrance (i.e., at the maximum condensed-phase [Caprin1]) is much higher with monovalent than with divalent counterions ([Na+] ∼ 1 M vs. ∼ 0.1 M).
evidence: This is a prediction from rG-RPA comparing Figure 2a,b with Figure 2e,f.

claim: [Na+] is depleted in the Caprin1 condensate with both monovalent and divalent counterions when overall [Na+] is high.
source: (iii) [Na+] is depleted in the Caprin1 condensate with both monovalent and divalent counterions when overall [Na+] is high (negative tieline slopes for [Na+] ≳ 2 M in Figure 2a and e).
evidence: This is a prediction from rG-RPA shown in Figure 2a and e.

claim: For lower overall [Na+], [Na+] is slightly higher in the Caprin1 condensate with divalent but not with monovalent counterions.
source: However, for lower overall [Na+], [Na+] is slightly higher in the Caprin1 condensate with divalent but not with monovalent counterions (slightly positive tieline slopes for [Na+] ≲ 2 M in Figure 2e and f).
evidence: This is a prediction from rG-RPA shown in Figure 2e and f.

claim: Under physiological [Na+] = 150∼170 mM, monovalent positive salt ions such as Na+ can be attracted into biomolecular condensates scaffolded by positively charged polyelectrolytic IDRs in the presence of divalent counterions.
source: This prediction suggests that under physiological [Na+] = 150∼170 mM, monovalent positive salt ions such as Na+ can be attracted, somewhat counterintuitively, into biomolecular condensates scaffolded by positively charged polyelectrolytic IDRs in the presence of divalent counterions.
evidence: This is an inference from the rG-RPA predictions about tieline slopes.

claim: Tetravalent counterions increase the theoretical maximum condensed-phase [Caprin1] to ≳ 120 mM.
source: Tetravalent counterions also increase the theoretical maximum condensed-phase [Caprin1] to ≳ 120 mM.
evidence: This is a prediction from rG-RPA shown in Figure 2i-l.

claim: All tieline slopes for Mg2+ and ATP4− are significantly positive, except in an extremely high-salt region with [Mg2+] > 8 M.
source: All tieline slopes for Mg2+ and ATP4− in Figure 2i–l are significantly positive, except in an extremely high-salt region with [Mg2+] > 8 M, indicating that [(ATP-Mg)2−] is almost always substantially enhanced in the Caprin1 condensate.
evidence: This is a prediction from rG-RPA shown in Figure 2i-l.

claim: [(ATP-Mg)2−] is almost always substantially enhanced in the Caprin1 condensate.
source: All tieline slopes for Mg2+ and ATP4− in Figure 2i–l are significantly positive, except in an extremely high-salt region with [Mg2+] > 8 M, indicating that [(ATP-Mg)2−] is almost always substantially enhanced in the Caprin1 condensate.
evidence: This is inferred from the positive tieline slopes in rG-RPA predictions in Figure 2i-l.

claim: rG-RPA-predicted semi-quantitative trends are consistent with experiments indicating [ATP-Mg]-dependent reentrant phase behavior of Caprin1.
source: Despite the tendency for polymer field theories to overestimate LLPS propensity and condensed-phase concentrations quantitatively because they do not account for ion condensation (Shen and Wang, 2017)—which can be severe for small ions with more than ±1 charge valencies as in the case of condensed [Caprin1] ≳ 120 mM in Figure 2i–l, our present rG-RPA-predicted semi-quantitative trends are consistent with experiments indicating [ATP-Mg]-dependent reentrant phase behavior of Caprin1 (Figure 3a, red data points, and Figure 3b) and that [Mg2+] as well as [ATP4−] are significantly enhanced in the Caprin1 condensate by a factor of ∼5–60 for overall [ATP-Mg] = 3–30 mM (Table 2).
evidence: This is a comparison between rG-RPA predictions and experimental data in Figure 3a, 3b, and Table 2.

claim: [Mg2+] and [ATP4−] are significantly enhanced in the Caprin1 condensate by a factor of ∼5–60 for overall [ATP-Mg] = 3–30 mM.
source: Despite the tendency for polymer field theories to overestimate LLPS propensity and condensed-phase concentrations quantitatively because they do not account for ion condensation (Shen and Wang, 2017)—which can be severe for small ions with more than ±1 charge valencies as in the case of condensed [Caprin1] ≳ 120 mM in Figure 2i–l, our present rG-RPA-predicted semi-quantitative trends are consistent with experiments indicating [ATP-Mg]-dependent reentrant phase behavior of Caprin1 (Figure 3a, red data points, and Figure 3b) and that [Mg2+] as well as [ATP4−] are significantly enhanced in the Caprin1 condensate by a factor of ∼5–60 for overall [ATP-Mg] = 3–30 mM (Table 2).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Table 2.

claim: Explicit-ion coarse-grained MD results show [NaCl]-dependent reentrant phase behavior for Caprin1 but not for pY-Caprin1.
source: Consistent with experiment (Figure 3) and rG-RPA (Figure 2a–d), explicit-ion coarse-grained MD results in Figure 4 show [NaCl]-dependent reentrant phase behavior for Caprin1 but not for pY-Caprin1 (non-monotonic and monotonic trends indicated, respectively, by the grey arrows in Figure 4a and b).
evidence: This is a result from MD simulations shown in Figure 4 and is consistent with experiment and rG-RPA.

claim: Na+ is slightly depleted in the Caprin1 condensed droplet according to MD simulations.
source: Moreover, consistent with the rG-RPA-predicted tielines in Figure 2a–d (negative slopes for Caprin1 and positive slopes for pY-Caprin1), Figure 4e and g show that Na+ is slightly depleted in the Caprin1 condensed droplet, exhibiting the same trend as that in experiment (Figure 3a, blue data points; and Table 1) but is enhanced in the pY-Caprin1 droplet (Figure 4f and h).
evidence: This is a result from MD simulations shown in Figure 4e and g and is consistent with experiment and rG-RPA.

claim: Na+ is enhanced in the pY-Caprin1 droplet according to MD simulations.
source: Moreover, consistent with the rG-RPA-predicted tielines in Figure 2a–d (negative slopes for Caprin1 and positive slopes for pY-Caprin1), Figure 4e and g show that Na+ is slightly depleted in the Caprin1 condensed droplet, exhibiting the same trend as that in experiment (Figure 3a, blue data points; and Table 1) but is enhanced in the pY-Caprin1 droplet (Figure 4f and h).
evidence: This is a result from MD simulations shown in Figure 4f and h.

claim: [Cl–] is enhanced while [Na+] is depleted in the Caprin1 droplet according to MD simulations.
source: Figure 4e and g show that [Cl–] is enhanced while [Na+] is depleted in the Caprin1 droplet.
evidence: This is a result from MD simulations shown in Figure 4e and g.

claim: Both [Cl–] and [Na+] are enhanced in the pY-Caprin1 droplet with an excess of [Na+] to balance the negatively charged pY-Caprin1.
source: By comparison, Figure 4f and h show that both [Cl–] and [Na+] are enhanced in the pY-Caprin1 droplet with an excess of [Na+] to balance the negatively charged pY-Caprin1 (Figure 4h).
evidence: This is a result from MD simulations shown in Figure 4f and h.

claim: Cl– can coordinate two positively charged R residues and thereby stabilize indirect counterion-bridged interchain contacts among polycationic Caprin1 molecules to promote LLPS.
source: For Caprin1, Figure 5e and f suggests that, as counterion, Cl– can coordinate two positively charged R residues and thereby stabilize indirect counterion-bridged interchain contacts among polycationic Caprin1 molecules to promote LLPS, consistent with an early lattice-model analysis of generic polyelectrolytes (Orkoulas et al., 2003) and a recent atomic simulation study of A1-LCD (MacAinsh et al., 2024).
evidence: This is inferred from MD simulation snapshots in Figure 5e and f and is consistent with prior theoretical and simulation work.

claim: 98.5% of the Cl– ions are within 11 Å of an Arg+ in the analyzed MD ensemble.
source: Indeed, within the ensemble we analyze, 5,121,148/(4000×1300) = 98.5% of the Cl– ions are within 11 Å of an Arg+.
evidence: This is a calculation from MD simulation data shown in Figure 6.

claim: 86.9% of the Cl– counterions are identified to be in one or more putative bridging interaction configurations.
source: In our ensemble, 4,519,387/(4000×1300) = 86.9% of the Cl– counterions are identified to be in one or more of a total of 25,112,331 such putative bridging interaction configurations.
evidence: This is a calculation from MD simulation data shown in Figure 6.

claim: On average, each Cl– is involved in 5.56 putative bridging configurations and is coordinating ≈ 4 Arg+s.
source: This means that, on average, each Cl– is involved in 25,112,331/4,519,387 = 5.56 configurations, and thus are coordinating ≈ 4 Arg+s because there are 6 (≈5.56) ways of pairing 4 Arg+s.
evidence: This is a calculation from MD simulation data.

claim: ≈80% of putative bridging configurations are true bridging configurations.
source: Even with this more stringent criterion, ≈80% of putative bridging configurations are true bridging configurations.
evidence: This is a result from analysis of MD simulation data shown in Figure 6c.

claim: An overwhelming majority (≈ 87%) of Cl− counterions in the coarse-grained MD system are engaged in condensation-driving true bridging interactions coordinating pairs of Arg+ on different Caprin1 chains.
source: Thus, even without taking into consideration bridging interactions involving lysines, we may reasonably conclude that an overwhelming majority (≈ 87%) of Cl− counterions in the coarse-grained MD system considered are engaged in condensation-driving true bridging interactions coordinating pairs of Arg+ on different Caprin1 chains.
evidence: This is inferred from the analysis of MD simulation data in Figure 6.

claim: MD simulations exhibit reentrant phase behaviors for all three 4Rto4K variants.
source: The simulated phase diagrams in Figure 7 exhibit reentrant phase behaviors for all three 4Rto4K variants.
evidence: This is a result from MD simulations shown in Figure 7.

claim: The simulated reentrant dissolution for 4Rto4K variants is not observed experimentally, probably because the actual [NaCl] needed is beyond the experimentally investigated or physically possible range of salt concentration.
source: While these results are consistent with experiments showing LLPS of these 4Rto4K variants commencing at different nonzero [NaCl]s (Wong et al., 2020), the simulated reentrant dissolution is not observed experimentally, probably because the actual [NaCl] needed is beyond the experimentally investigated or physically possible range of salt concentration.
evidence: This is an inference to explain the discrepancy between simulation and experiment.

claim: The MD prediction that the highest Tcr for 15Rto15K is essentially at the same level as Tcr0 for WT at [NaCl] = 0 is consistent with the combined experimental observations of no LLPS for 15Rto15K up to at least [NaCl] = 2 M and no LLPS for WT Caprin1 at [NaCl] = 0.
source: This MD prediction is consistent with the combined experimental observations of no LLPS for 15Rto15K up to at least [NaCl] = 2 M and no LLPS for WT Caprin1 at [NaCl] = 0 (Figure 9B and C of Wong et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a comparison between MD simulation predictions in Figure 7a and experimental data.

claim: FTS consistently shows reentrant behavior for Caprin1 but not pY-Caprin1.
source: Despite these variations in FTS models, Appendix 1—figures 4–6 consistently show reentrant behavior for Caprin1 but not pY-Caprin1 and Appendix 1—figures 5 and 6 both exhibit colocalization of ATP with condensed Caprin1, suggesting that these features are robust consequences of the basic electrostatics at play in Caprin1/pY-Caprin1 + ATP-Mg + NaCl systems.
evidence: This is a result from FTS shown in Figures 8 and 9 and Appendix figures.

claim: FTS exhibits colocalization of ATP with condensed Caprin1.
source: Despite these variations in FTS models, Appendix 1—figures 4–6 consistently show reentrant behavior for Caprin1 but not pY-Caprin1 and Appendix 1—figures 5 and 6 both exhibit colocalization of ATP with condensed Caprin1, suggesting that these features are robust consequences of the basic electrostatics at play in Caprin1/pY-Caprin1 + ATP-Mg + NaCl systems.
evidence: This is a result from FTS shown in Figures 8 and 9 and Appendix figures.

claim: The residue-position-dependent integrated correlation for (ATP-Mg)2− varies significantly, exhibiting much larger values near the N-terminal and a little before the C-terminal but weaker correlation elsewhere.
source: Notably, the residue-position-dependent integrated correlation for (ATP-Mg)2− varies significantly, exhibiting much larger values near the N-terminal and a little before the C-terminal but weaker correlation elsewhere (Figure 8f, red symbols).
evidence: This is a result from FTS shown in Figure 8f.

claim: The two regions of high integrated correlation for (ATP-Mg)2− coincide with regions with high sequence concentration of positively charged residues.
source: The two regions of high integrated correlation (i.e., favorable association) coincide with regions with high sequence concentration of positively charged residues.
evidence: This is inferred from comparing the FTS results in Figure 8f with the sequence in Figure 1a.

claim: Colocalization of (ATP-Mg)2− with both the Caprin1 and pY-Caprin1 droplets is clearly visible at [(ATP-Mg)2−] = 0.03b−3.
source: Colocalization of (ATP-Mg)2− with both the Caprin1 (Figure 9c) and pY-Caprin1 (Figure 9d) droplets is clearly visible at [(ATP-Mg)2−] = 0.03b−3, though the degree of colocalization is appreciably higher for Caprin1 than for pY-Caprin1.
evidence: This is a result from FTS snapshots shown in Figure 9c and d.

claim: The degree of (ATP-Mg)2− colocalization is appreciably higher for Caprin1 than for pY-Caprin1.

claim: Full-length Caprin1 is a ubiquitously expressed phosphoprotein that regulates stress and neuronal granules.
source: Full-length Caprin1 (709 amino acid residues) is a ubiquitously expressed phosphoprotein that regulates stress (Solomon et al., 2007; Towers et al., 2011; Vu et al., 2021; Song et al., 2022) and neuronal (El Fatimy et al., 2012) granules, is necessary for normal cellular proliferation (Ellis and Luzio, 1995; Wang et al., 2005), and may be essential for long-term memory (Nakayama et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: Caprin1 dysfunction leads to multiple diseases such as nasopharyngeal carcinoma as well as language impairment and autism spectrum disorder.
source: Caprin1 dysfunction leads to multiple diseases such as nasopharyngeal carcinoma (Yang et al., 2022) as well as language impairment and autism spectrum disorder (Pavinato et al., 2023), via, for example, Caprin1's modulation of the function of the fragile X mental retardation protein (FMRP; Tsang et al., 2019; Kim et al., 2019; El Fatimy et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The C-terminal 607–709 Caprin1 IDR is sufficient for LLPS in vitro.
source: The C-terminal 607–709 Caprin1 IDR, referred to simply as Caprin1 below, is biophysically and functionally significant: It is sufficient for LLPS in vitro (Kim et al., 2019), important for assembling stress granules in the cell (Solomon et al., 2007; Towers et al., 2011), and has a substantial body of experiments (Kim et al., 2019; Wong et al., 2020; Kim et al., 2021; Toyama et al., 2022) for comparison with theory.
evidence: This is supported by citation to experimental work.

claim: Tyrosine phosphorylations of Caprin1 in vivo may regulate translation in neurons.
source: Since tyrosine phosphorylations of Caprin1 in vivo (Hornbeck et al., 2015) may regulate translation in neurons (Kim et al., 2019), the Caprin1 system is also useful for gaining insights into phosphoregulation of biomolecular condensates (Monahan et al., 2017; Dignon et al., 2018; Carlson et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a speculative claim supported by citations.
